ds: Fishing in breach of licence, quota or location rules, often with transhipment at sea, vessel identity changes and forced labour on board. The catch is mixed into legal supply and sold via processors, traders and retailers.

src.t: UNODC, Transnational Organized Crime in the Fishing Industry (2011)
FATF, Money Laundering from Environmental Crime (2021)
FAO, Agreement on Port State Measures to Prevent, Deter and Eliminate Illegal, Unreported and Unregulated Fishing (2009, in force 2016)
Interpol, public material on fisheries crime

rat: Vessel owners, traders and processors with seafood trade finance, vessel insurance and crew payments through agencies.

ind.n: Vessel with history of AIS gaps or name and flag changes
ind.cx: Vessel switches off position tracking, changes names or flags often and is on IUU lists.
ind.fp: Technical faults and legitimate re-flagging occur.
ind.ds: Vessel switches off position tracking, changes names or flags often and is on IUU lists.

ind.n: Payments for at-sea transhipment, fuel and supplies
ind.cx: Payments to reefer ships or bunker suppliers in remote waters.
ind.fp: Transhipment is lawful under authorised conditions.
ind.ds: Payments to reefer ships or bunker suppliers in remote waters.

ind.n: Catch documentation inconsistent with vessel capacity or licence
ind.cx: Landing volumes or species exceed capacity, quota or fishing area.
ind.ds: Landing volumes or species exceed capacity, quota or fishing area.

ind.n: Ownership by layered offshore companies and flags of convenience
ind.cx: Vessels owned via shell companies in secrecy jurisdictions with unclear controllers.
ind.ds: Multiple tiers of entities, trusts or foundations, often across secrecy or low-transparency jurisdictions, with no evident business or tax reason.
ind.cn: Complex layered structure without commercial rationale

ind.n: Crew payments below standards or via third parties
ind.cx: Crew recruited by agencies with fees, wages held back, or payments to agents.
ind.ds: Crew recruited by agencies with fees, wages held back, or payments to agents.

ind.n: Seafood sales through traders with no traceability
ind.cx: Processors or exporters cannot show the vessel or catch origin.
ind.fp: Smaller traders may lack digital records.
ind.ds: Processors or exporters cannot show the vessel or catch origin.

ind.n: Port calls in ports of low inspection standards
ind.cx: Frequent landings at ports with weak controls or non-parties to port state measures.
ind.fp: Ports may be the only option for some fleets.
ind.ds: Frequent landings at ports with weak controls or non-parties to port state measures.

ind.n: Adverse media or enforcement for IUU activity
ind.cx: Vessel, owner or manager in sanction or prosecution lists.
ind.ds: Credible negative news, enforcement notices or investigations link the customer, its owners or associates to criminal, corrupt or regulated-sector misconduct.
ind.cn: Adverse media on customer or associates

ctl.ds: Runs continuous screening of customers, owners, introducers, suppliers and counterparties against curated news, leaks, regulatory notices and enforcement releases, with reliability grading and identity disambiguation. It surfaces negative information that registers and lists do not carry.

Compares shipping routes, ports and delivery points with typical lanes and risk lists, and requests explanation for unusual hubs or indirect delivery. It reveals diversion, transshipment and evasion routing.

ctl.n: Vessel due diligence and tracking analytics
ctl.ds: Verifies vessel identity, ownership, flag history, insurance and class, and analyses tracking data for gaps, loitering, ship-to-ship transfers and spoofing. It addresses sanctions and illicit-trade evasion at sea.

ctl.n: Licence and permit verification for regulated goods
ctl.ds: Validates licences, permits, certificates and authorisations with the issuing authority and compares their scope with observed activity or shipments. It prevents genuine permits being misused or forged permits being accepted.

Compares reported volumes with capacity, production, mass balance, concession size and national trade statistics to test whether quantities are physically possible. It exposes inflated, laundered or mislabelled flows.

Identifies the natural persons who ultimately own or control a legal entity or arrangement and verifies them using independent registers and documents, looking through intermediate layers. It is the core defence against anonymity achieved through layered or opaque structures.

ctl.n: Country, corridor and port risk rating framework
ctl.ds: Maintains documented risk ratings of countries, corridors, ports and booking centres drawn from transparency, corruption and mutual-evaluation sources, updated on a schedule and after relevant events. The ratings feed due diligence, monitoring and limits.

ctl.n: Labour provider and recruiter due diligence
ctl.ds: Verifies licences, ownership, registration, tax compliance and wage-payment evidence of labour providers and recruiters at onboarding and review, and checks recruitment practices. It reduces exposure to exploitative labour supply and undeclared work.

Provides discreet escalation routes and private conversation procedures so staff can refer suspected victims of exploitation, coercion or trafficking to specialists, police and support organisations. It prioritises victim safety.

Audits suppliers and processors, including interviews and records, and requires corrective action plans and remediation with support for affected workers. It verifies conditions on the ground and drives fixes rather than only detecting problems.

Maps suppliers and sub-suppliers back through the chain, down to plot, mine or farm level where relevant, and requires traceability of key inputs to origin. It makes hidden high-risk sources visible so they can be excluded or audited.
Participates in sector, regulator and public-private forums and platform cooperation to receive and share typologies and indicators where lawful. It keeps scenarios current.
